content: Toronto East General Hospital is a teaching hospital situated in Toronto, Ontario, within the area formerly known as East York. The hospital is equipped with 382 acute care beds, 13 beds dedicated to rehabilitation, and 75 beds for complex continuing care. During the 2006/07 fiscal year, the hospital managed over 60,000 visits to its emergency department and admitted more than 19,000 patients for in-patient care. Within the same period, approximately 3,500 babies were delivered at the hospital's Maternal Newborn and Child Health Centre. This centre specializes in providing Level II Maternity and Neonatal Care and serves as a regional pediatric hub within the Child Health Network of Toronto. The hospital's chief of staff is Dr. Alfio Meschino, while its president and CEO is Rob Devitt. The hospital offers a wide range of services, including: Ambulatory and community-based healthcare services. Care for patients requiring complex continuing care and short-term rehabilitation. Emergency medical services. Comprehensive maternal, newborn, and child health services. General and specialized medical care. Mental health services. Pharmaceutical services. Surgical procedures and perioperative care. Diagnostic imaging services, such as X-rays, CT scans, and MRIs. Laboratory medicine for diagnostic testing and analysis.
